items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: Interviewer mentions Sid Catlett; Interviewee responds 'That he could do it' referring to Catlett's ability, but no direct interaction or personal relationship is stated by the interviewee.

ctx.x: Yeah. And very few people -- now when they give the drummer a course, it seems to me that they just want to rest for a while.
Sid Catlett was the first one that impressed me as being so musical, you could hear the changes in the tune.

That he could do it. Very few can do it today, in my opinion, again. But anyway, I'm finally at Rind's and I'm finally invited to play, one Sunday afternoon. It wasn't a big deal. I think I paid either seven or ten dollars. I remember playing City College and I hired Eddie Condon, Mezz Crow, Cliff Jackson, Frankie Newton and Dave Tough at seven dollars apiece, on Collins Stage, and I got ten for being leader and getting them together.

items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: And they had started with people like Bechet, Sidney Bechet, and Big Sid Catlett and Joe Sullivan and Doc Evans.

ctx.x: To get back to it, I was finding out that to keep a band, you had to go out on the road because there wasn't enough places in Chicago to play. R. U. neck's -- then Danny Alvin got the job at R. U. neck's or somebody else. Johnny Lane. There was a few leaders all fighting for the same work. And so about 1953, I ran out of work for bands. And that means I had to do something. So I went to work at Jazz Limited, which was a new experience.

There was a club that played music, no dancing. And they had started with people like Bechet, Sidney Bechet, and Big Sid Catlett and Joe Sullivan and Doc Evans. They've had some main people. And now they were down to just using one or two local names without importing. And salaries were -- well, you were getting a weekly stipend that's not great, but it's certainly scale or over.

And you were playing jazz music of a kind. I mean, it's not what you would choose to play all the time. Occasionally you'd get to play some you would choose to play. And the tempos are not what you would choose to play. It's the leader, the leader sets the style and the leader owns the club. So you go along, if you want the job.
